newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major reiterates warning on single currency.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major reiterates warning on single currency.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Saturday reiterated a warning against rushing into a single European currency saying it could cause serious damage if the economic conditions were not right.

"If it goes wrong because people go in because it is their political will to do so when it is not economically sensible ... then the damage right across Europe will be very serious indeed," Major told BBC radio in an interview.

Speaking in Dublin, where the new euro banknote was unveiled on Friday and European Union leaders agreed a pact on future budget discipline, Major said there was still doubt about the system beginning on time in January 1999.
He said the real question was not whether other member states could go ahead but whether they would be economically ready.
"No one can be certain about that. I have some doubts about whether they will be safely ready to go ahead.
"I think they would be very unwise to go ahead without the right economic circumstances," Major said.

He said it was in Britain's national interest to ensure that the single currency was a success if it went ahead -- whether or not Britain decided to join -- because it would inevitably feel the effect of the system.

Major on Friday reaffirmed that Britain would take a wait-and-see attitude to joining the euro and also cast doubt on a European Union declaration to coordinate the fight against unemployment, currently running at 18.5 million in the EU.
